topic: Strategy in the age of AI: a talk with Alex Reed
title: Strategy in the age of AI: a talk with Alex Reed
lead: The keynote is over. You walk up to Alex Reed, the founder of a company rebuilt around AI, and talk business strategy over coffee. In each turn, two of the four replies are correct, and they say different things. Choose the one that sounds like you.
how: You are a guest at a conference. Choose what you say.
In each turn two replies are correct and two have a slip in grammar, word choice or tone. Pick the one that is yours.
A red ✕ shows a slip and the corrected sentence. Tap an underlined word to see what it means. Right the first time? You get a star ★.

words.definition: the main speech at the start of a conference
words.example: The keynote is over and the hall is slowly emptying.

words.definition: to make a process simpler and faster
words.example: Many firms only use AI to streamline what they already do.

words.definition: a small test of a new idea before a company uses it everywhere
words.example: We're running a few small pilots, nothing more.

words.definition: to start using something new in the whole company
words.example: We've already rolled out AI in customer support.

words.definition: to make a job happen by machine, without people doing it
words.example: The biggest risk is automating the wrong thing.

words.definition: something that puts your company ahead of the others
words.example: AI is only a competitive edge if it changes how people work.

words.definition: a step in a process where work slows down because too much arrives
words.example: I'd begin with the bottlenecks, the steps where work always piles up.

words.definition: the support and agreement of the people who have to accept a change
words.example: Buy-in from the team matters more than the tool.

words.definition: to start using a new idea or tool
words.example: How do you get people to adopt it?

words.definition: all the people who work for a company or in an industry
words.example: Will AI make the workforce shrink?
The market may shrink next year.

words.definition: to teach people new skills for their job
words.example: The bigger task is to upskill people rather than replace them.

words.definition: to contact someone again after a first meeting
words.example: Would it be all right if I followed up by email?
